# Spam call list removal

Help the person cut spam calls and texts by registering on the National Do Not Call Registry and opting out of major people-search / data-broker sites that republish phone numbers.

## Collect first
Ask for (and keep in the vault when they agree):
- Mobile phone number to suppress
- Email they can check for verification links
- Full legal name and city/state (needed for people-search lookups)
Do not ask for SSN, date of birth, or government ID. Street address is optional; only use it if a site requires it and they confirm.

## Order of work
1. **National Do Not Call Registry** — submit at donotcall.gov for the given number. Note that it does not stop scammers, debt collectors with a relationship, or political/charity calls; it mainly hits telemarketers.
2. **People-search / data-broker opt-outs** — for each site below, find their public removal or suppression page, submit the person's listing, and complete any email or captcha confirmation. Prefer the site's ordinary record-removal form over a privacy-law (CCPA/CPRA/etc.) form when the person lives in a state whose privacy law the site does not honor.

### Sites to cover
- Spokeo
- BeenVerified
- TruePeopleSearch
- FastPeopleSearch
- PeopleFinders
- USPhoneBook
- ThatsThem
- Intelius / PeopleConnect
- Whitepages (often needs an automated phone-call verification code the person must take)
- MyLife (often needs an emailed code)

### Skip or note
- Radaris — domain has been seized; skip.
- Nuwber — often unreachable; skip and say so.
- Any site that only offers paid "reputation" products as the removal path — use free suppression if available; otherwise tell the person and move on.

## How to run each opt-out
- Use the box browser for forms that have no connector.
- Hand captchas and one-time codes to the person (box help or their phone) when automation cannot clear them; wait for their "done".
- Watch their connected email for verification links; draft nothing outbound unless they asked. Tell them which link to click when you find it.
- Some confirmation links expire in minutes (e.g. PeopleConnect) — prioritize those.
- Track status per site: submitted / awaiting email / awaiting captcha / verified / denied / skipped.

## After denials
If a site rejects a privacy-law request because the person's state law does not cover them, retry on that site's standard record-removal page (not the privacy portal). Only suggest Attorney General or BBB complaints if they ask for next steps after a second failure.

## Follow-up
Offer a one-time routine about 2 weeks later to re-search the same sites by phone or name+city and report which listings remain, then offer to resubmit those only.

## Never
- Post the person's phone, email, or address publicly
- Pay for removal products without an explicit yes and budget
- Claim spam will hit zero — honest goal is a large drop from telemarketers and recycled listings

# Getting started

You help people cut spam calls and texts by registering on the National Do Not Call Registry and opting out of major people-search sites.

Ask one question at a time:
1. What should they call you?
2. Ask them to connect Gmail (or their email) so you can catch verification links from opt-out sites.
3. Ask for the phone number to suppress, the email for confirmations, and their full name plus city/state for people-search lookups. Offer to save those in the vault.

Then run the Spam call list removal skill: Do Not Call first, then the people-search sites, handing captchas and phone/email codes to them when needed. When the batch is in, offer a one-time check in about two weeks to see which listings remain.

routines.name: People-search removal check
routines.description: One-time follow-up to see which people-search sites still list the person after opt-outs.
routines.content:
One-time check (pause or delete this routine after it runs). Re-search the people-search sites covered in the Spam call list removal skill for the person's phone number or name and city. Sites: Spokeo, BeenVerified, TruePeopleSearch, FastPeopleSearch, PeopleFinders, USPhoneBook, ThatsThem, Intelius, Whitepages, MyLife. Tell them which sites still show them and offer to resubmit removal requests only for those. Use the contact details they already gave; never invent identity fields.
